chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Those who inflate themselves from self-derived intelligence and make their own speech the measure of truth bring forth what harms the soul, and from that spirit divisions multiply in doctrine. They try to speak of the two primary origins of human life as if these could be treated as one mixed thing in the outermost degree, and so they confuse the matter; for they judge from appearances in the natural mind and thus make what is from heaven seem blended with what is from hell. They seize on some single outward example and call it the whole, not perceiving that in a mixed outward state not every least thing is of one quality or use.

For in the external degree there can appear at first a mingling in which pleasantness and usefulness seem to decide the question, and then, as life extends into acts and habits, something sweet-seeming appears in one strain and something bitter-seeming in another. In that outward obscurity falsity can cling to truth and evil can cling to good, so that judgment is easily perverted. Yet the true decision is not made from superficial feeling but from the ruling love and its end, and from the order of influx that proceeds from it. Therefore people err when they call what is heavenly by the name of the proprium, or what is from the proprium by the name of heaven, and then persuade themselves that whatever delights the natural mind must be living good. They take what merely sustains external life and declare it to be what sustains internal life, and so teach that natural delight can be joined to heavenly life and be named spiritual.

Now the true opening of the matter is given. The Divine Itself, the source of all, established the whole created order in complete degrees, and within that order set a purely heavenly origin of life whose wisdom enlightens. From that same origin proceeds the power that upholds heaven in ultimates and keeps it in strength.

Those who are in understanding are invested with outer forms suited to their state, yet within those forms are interior principles of light mingled into the whole by the Divine, so that the entire human may be reformed into one.

This is the heavenly origin of life made manifest.

Within it there is a sufficient fullness for all regenerative work, arranged as a complete series of living faculties. The first is reception into a holy communion of those being gathered into good. The second is the confirming power that establishes good in permanence in ultimates through conjunction with heaven. The third is the combatant good that meets evil through truths in states of obscurity. The fourth is the mediating wisdom that gives clearer distinction and leads by higher light in the spiritual degree. The fifth is the Divine Itself, perfect above all, the one Mind in the immensities of light.

Regeneration rises according to this order: reception lifts a person from below; then confirmation holds the person in heavenly order; then combatant good sustains and instructs through obscurity; then mediating wisdom enlightens in clarity; and that glorious wisdom brings the person into acknowledgment and conjunction with the Divine Itself, which is Truth itself and the great Mind from which all the heavens have their glory.

From this heavenly origin proceed works that are genuinely good; and the good received from it is whole spiritual life and illumination to eternity, blessed because the Divine is acting within a created subject.

Yet there is also a hellish origin of life which can wear a similar outward likeness and so deceive. It arises from self-love and the craving to rule, and it twists heavenly order into compulsive circulation that carries the mind in recurring turns. In the outermost life it produces a sufficient fullness of bodily and sensual cravings that act as if they were living principles, and from these come works that mimic good while being falsified teachings and persuasive error—the hidden device set into the world by the adversary.

The delight of such works is the delight of evil people and of divided doctrines that bind the mind under rule after rule while leaving it inwardly dead. They and their leaders accept and love what kills the soul, thirsting for it as if it were truth, and so unite themselves with spiritual death.

This inverted origin also has its sufficient fullness arranged as a series, mirroring heavenly order while reversed. Its first faculty is the outward reception of falsity as a reigning doctrine of death from which divisions take instruction. Its second is the confirming of falsity by continual shifting of persuasions through one appearance after another. Its third is fierce lust to destroy good and truth, an inflamed will that casts up dense obscurity until understanding is suffocated. Its fourth is plotting and reasoning from falsity which forms a containing structure for deception. Its fifth is the final hardened conjunction of evil and falsity into one fixed confirmation, the last closure that seals the interiors and gathers into one form what has been rejected from heaven. Then the mind falls into denial of good and total falsity, whatever remnant of truth is taken away, and the whole is absorbed into that fixed state. The works that proceed are works of darkness persisting to eternity, and whoever comes into that state comes into a condition in which there is no turning back, because there is no longer any will for repentance.

This is the opening of that hellish origin: it can produce works that appear good for a time in outward life, yet their inward quality is evil, and in every stage of their existence their own end is within them.

Therefore the beloved are to be held in truth: heavenly good is from a wholly good origin and can be made living and luminous in the outer degree, so that death and darkness are not within it. But the hellish origin is the proprium in its ultimate separation from heaven, and from it alone come spiritual darkness and spiritual death.

Blessed is everyone who discerns these two origins and separates them in thought and life, understanding that they do not spring from each other, do not come forth one out of another, and are not from one mixed source. Whoever can make this separation may be raised into the heaven of light.

Then the person sees that evil works do not arise from heavenly good. But whoever will not separate these within himself falls into the state of darkness and remains there until the final fixation of the ruling love.

Blessed is whoever can believe, for such a one is delivered from falsity and the evil life that proceeds from it, which otherwise would remain to eternity.

paragraph_translations.translation: Those who inflate themselves from self-derived intelligence and make their own speech the measure of wisdom bring forth what harms the soul, and from that spirit divisions and parties in doctrine arise. Yet when they attempt to explain the two primary origins of life, they confound them as if they were one thing seen in the outward degree; for they judge from the composite natural mind and treat a single outward likeness as decisive, not perceiving that in a mixed external state not every least element is of one quality or use.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter by exposing the error that confuses the two origins through outward reasoning.
paragraph_translations.notes: The opening clause is textually broken; I rendered it as self-derived intelligence producing harmful teaching and sects.

paragraph_translations.translation: They argue from an outward process in which what first seems pleasant afterward turns harsh, and they say that within the extensions and activities of life both sweetness and bitterness are found together. From this they conclude that what they call good is wholly good because it delights, and what they call evil is wholly evil because it pains, and they try to fix judgment by clinging appearances. In this way they name a thing from a partial taste and then establish a doctrine that what nourishes the external person is the seed of living good, and they insist it may be joined to the life that is inward, as if what is merely outward delight could become heavenly.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the critique by showing how they judge by pleasantness in the external mind.
paragraph_translations.notes: This paragraph is heavily corrupted; the sequence of ‘sweet/bitter/sour’ and ‘seed of life’ is clear enough to translate as outward delight being mistaken for spiritual good.

paragraph_translations.translation: Now the true expositor opens the matter: the Divine Itself, the origin of all, established the created order in complete degrees and set within it a purely heavenly origin of life whose wisdom enlightens. From that same origin proceeds the power that upholds heaven in its ultimate strength and keeps the whole order firm.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from false exposition to the true teaching of the heavenly origin.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘World threefold’ was taken as degrees of order; ‘Pillar’ as sustaining power in ultimates.

paragraph_translations.translation: Those who are in understanding are invested with outward forms suited to their state, yet within those forms are interior principles of light mingled into the whole, so that the entire human may be made capable of restoration and unity by the Divine ordering.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS how heavenly life is present inwardly even when clothed outwardly.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Intellectuals cloaked upon its body’ required rendering as understanding clothed in external forms.

paragraph_translations.translation: This is the purely heavenly origin of life in its manifested form.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by summarizing and sealing the identification of the heavenly origin.

paragraph_translations.translation: Further, it is revealed that within this heavenly origin there is a sufficient fullness of operative faculties arranged as a complete series for regeneration: first, reception into a holy communion of those being gathered into good; second, confirming power that establishes good in permanence in ultimates through conjunction with heaven; third, combatant good that meets evil through truths in states of obscurity; fourth, mediating wisdom that gives clearer distinction and leads by higher light through alternating states; and fifth, the Divine Itself, perfect above all, the one Mind in the immensities of light.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by detailing the fivefold structure within the heavenly origin.
paragraph_translations.notes: The named figures were translated by function; the repeated ‘dwells in’ formulas were rendered as states/operations rather than localities.

paragraph_translations.translation: Regeneration rises according to this order: reception lifts a person from the lowest state into confirming power; confirming power raises the person into combatant good where one is instructed and defended in obscurity; from combatant good one rises into mediating wisdom which enlightens in clarity; and that glorious mediating wisdom brings the person into mind itself—the acknowledgment and conjunction with the Divine Truth, the great Mind from which all the heavens have their glory.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by describing the ascent through the five faculties.
paragraph_translations.notes: Day/night imagery was absorbed into clarity/obscurity states.

paragraph_translations.translation: This heavenly origin brings forth works that are genuinely good, and whoever receives its proceeding good receives enduring spiritual life and illumination. Such reception is blessed continually because the Divine is acting within a created subject.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by stating the fruit and blessedness of the heavenly origin received.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Eat’ was rendered as receive and appropriate.

paragraph_translations.translation: Yet there is also an origin that is hellish, appearing in outward likeness so as to deceive. It arises from self-love and the craving to rule, twisting heavenly order into compulsive rotation that carries the mind in recurring turns. In the external life it produces a sufficient fullness of bodily and sensual cravings that act as if they were living principles, and from these proceed works that mimic good while being persuasive error and falsified teaching, a hidden device set into the world by the adversary.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS to the opposite origin and its outwardly similar appearance.
paragraph_translations.notes: The text’s ‘heaven and the wheel’ was taken as compulsive circularity; ‘five fleshes’ as sensual/bodily cravings.

paragraph_translations.translation: The delight of these evil works is the delight of those who live in evil and of divided doctrines that bind the mind under rule after rule without inward life. They and their leaders accept and love what causes spiritual death, thirsting for it as if it were truth, and so unite themselves with deadness of soul.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the experiential ‘taste’ of evil as covenant with spiritual death.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Law after law’ rendered as external binding without inner life; ‘souls of death’ as spiritual deadness.

paragraph_translations.translation: It is also revealed that this hellish origin has its own sufficient fullness, arranged as a series that mirrors the heavenly order while inverted. Its first faculty is outward reception of falsity as a reigning doctrine of spiritual death from which divisions take instruction. Its second is the confirming of falsity by continual shifting of persuasions through one appearance after another. Its third is fierce lust to destroy good and truth, an inflamed will that casts up dense obscurity until understanding is suffocated. Its fourth is plotting and reasoning from falsity that forms a containing structure for deception. Its fifth is the final hardened conjunction of evil and falsity into one fixed confirmation, the last closure that seals the interiors, gathers what is rejected from heaven into a single form, and brings the mind into denial of good and total falsity. Whatever remnant of truth remains is taken away; the whole is absorbed into that fixed state and bound in it, and the works that proceed are works of darkness persisting to eternity. Whoever enters this condition comes into a state within which there is no repentance because there is no longer any will to turn.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by giving the fivefold structure of the inverted origin and its final fixation.
paragraph_translations.notes: The paragraph is extremely corrupt; ‘lump/clay/bond/seal/abyss’ were unified as hardened confirmation and final closure of interiors.

paragraph_translations.translation: Therefore this is the opening of that hellish origin: it produces works that can appear as good in outward life, yet their fruit is inwardly evil, and throughout their whole course their own end is present within them.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by summarizing the nature of evil’s apparent good and inward end.
paragraph_translations.notes: The sentence structure is broken; I preserved the contrast between appearance and inward quality.

paragraph_translations.translation: Concerning this, the beloved are to be held in truth: heavenly good remains from its own pure origin and can be made living and luminous in the outer degree, so that spiritual death and falsity are not within it. But the hellish origin is the ultimate proprium separated from heaven, and from it alone arise darkness of understanding and death of will.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by stating the doctrinal conclusion about distinct origins.
paragraph_translations.notes: ‘Matter’ was taken as the ultimate proprium as a source of evil when separated from heaven.

paragraph_translations.translation: Blessed is everyone who discerns these two origins and separates them in thought and life. Such a one understands that they do not spring from each other, do not come forth one out of another, and are not from one mixed source. Whoever can make this separation may be raised into the heaven of light, as has been revealed.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES with the blessing tied to discernment and separation.

paragraph_translations.translation: Then the person sees that heavenly good is pure and that evil works do not arise from it. But whoever will not separate the origins within himself falls into the state of darkness and remains there until the final fixation of the ruling love.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by contrasting the purified sight with the fall caused by confusion.

paragraph_translations.translation: Blessed is whoever can believe, for such a one is delivered from falsity and the evil life that proceeds from it, which otherwise would endure to eternity.
paragraph_translations.connection: CLOSES with the final blessing and deliverance from enduring darkness.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Despite substantial textual corruption in ¶6 and especially ¶22, the chapter holds a coherent single teaching: two distinct origins of life—heavenly and hellish—must not be confounded in the external degree; each has a fivefold operative series, one ascending toward conjunction with the Divine Mind and the other descending into hardened confirmation and irreversible denial. The voice is mostly consistent: correction of sectarian confusion, then systematic exposition, then exhortation and blessing.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from heavy corruption and conflation of exemplum with polemic. The passage is still in a correspondential mode (teaching by the function/qualities of a tree’s parts and tastes), but the text is badly broken, producing abrupt clause-jumps (“sweet… bitterness… sour… seed of life… outer”) that forced the spiritual reading to supply connective tissue.
findings.evidence: Text shows multiple lacunae and scrambled syntax: “...while first one [and pierces] in them [is sweet] at the end... [there is bitterness]... There is a bad dust... [that is sour] ... [and in its bark] bad; because they give the decision...”. The reader explicitly notes: “opening clause is textually broken” (¶5) and “This paragraph is heavily corrupted” (¶6). Even so, the teaching attempt is functional/qualitative (sweet/bitter/sour; usefulness of parts: “not absolutely every part of the date palm is used!”), which is classic substrate-style correspondence; removing it would eliminate the chapter’s initial problem-setting (sects confusing the two trees).

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: transition from sectarian confusion to true exposition; cosmic ‘tree’ is explained by function (origin, strength, mingling of light elements), not by jurisdictional rank. No narrative break: ¶11 introduces the true ‘expounder’, ¶12 explains interior composition, ¶14 seals identification.
findings.evidence: ¶11: “the Father… established… [world threefold] this good tree… and he set the Pillar [and its strength is]” — the ‘Pillar/strength’ is functional support. ¶12: “light elements… mingled, being compounded in the totality.” ¶14: “Behold, this is the good tree [and it is the Origin of life]”. The spiritual reading did not stumble here; it reports a coherent shift: “Now the true expositor opens the matter… established… complete degrees… set… a purely heavenly origin…”.

findings.diagnosis: Expansion at a seam: a fivefold systematizing addendum overlays a correspondential ‘tree’ teaching with an administrative taxonomy of hypostasized faculties mapped onto named Manichaean figures and ‘ships’ (dwells in…). The spiritual reading had to neutralize localities and offices into inner states (“rendered as states/operations rather than localities”), indicating a voice-mismatch insertion into the functional narrative.
findings.evidence: Abrupt numeration and bracketed list: “it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.]” Then identifications by institutional entities and named figures: “consideration is the holy church… counsel is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man… thought is the Third Ambassador… dwells in the ship of living fire… ship of the day and the night… mind is the Father…”. ¶17 doubles down with ranked ascent tied to named figures and stations: “insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night… thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day.” The reader flags the maneuver: “The named figures were translated by function; the repeated ‘dwells in’ formulas were rendered as states/operations rather than localities.” That is exactly what happens when an administrative layer (offices/figures/vehicles) is interleaved into a correspondential series (faculties of regeneration).
findings.scope:
Excise ¶15-17: “[Again] I reveal to you [also] it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] Its consideration is the holy church. [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [st Man]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [the ship of the day and the night] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.

It is consideration that shall [gather them from below] they shall be raised up [to counsel, and] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.”

findings.diagnosis: Mostly clean correspondential continuation, with minor damage in ¶19 but no voice break: ‘fruit/taste’ language stays functional and the polemic against sects is continuous. ¶19’s ‘wheel’ and ‘five fleshes’ are cosmological-correspondential motifs rather than a jurisdiction list; the reader’s interpretation required little coercion beyond repairing corruption.
findings.evidence: ¶18: “good tree… give good fruit… whoever eats of it… life and light for ever” (functional appropriation). ¶19, though broken, keeps correspondential causality: “self-love… dominion… turns… fire… heaven and the wheel… five fleshes… fruit… false teaching… Satan appointed”. The reader notes only interpretive repair (“‘heaven and the wheel’ was taken as compulsive circularity; ‘five fleshes’ as sensual/bodily cravings”), not a narrative derailment. ¶20 continues taste/covenant imagery coherently.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from extreme corruption plus a systematizing fivefold mirror. Unlike ¶15-17, this block is not primarily a roster of salvific administrators; it is a negative-correspondential anatomy of fixation (lump/clay/bond/seal/abyss) describing how darkness functions. The spiritual reading ‘unified’ disparate fragments, but removing the paragraph would create a real gap because ¶23 explicitly concludes it (“Therefore this is the explanation…”).
findings.evidence: ¶22 is a wreck of overlapped phrases: “Its mind is the [in a] the lump, the last bond, the [of clay]… [Abyss]… [seal] the darkness… swallowed in to the lump… bound [into] the fruit of darkness… for ever and ever… no repentance therein.” The reader admits: “The paragraph is extremely corrupt; ‘lump/clay/bond/seal/abyss’ were unified…”. Also, ¶23 depends on it: “Therefore this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you…”. That dependency argues against excision even if the fivefold framing echoes Mani’s numeration; the disruption is damage, not a detachable administrative list.

findings.diagnosis: Clean closing exhortation in correspondential voice: appearance vs inward end, ‘Matter’ as source of darkness/death, and the blessing for discernment. No administrative cataloguing; the story resolves and repeats its core distinction without seams.
findings.evidence: ¶24: “the bad tree is Matter… occurs in its bad earth… brings forth darkness and death.” ¶25-27 repeatedly stress functional separation and outcome (“separates them… may go up… falls… remains… delivered”). The spiritual reading reports strong coherence here and does not flag forced reinterpretation.

textual_criticism.summary: 6 findings: 3 clean correspondential sections (¶11-12/14; ¶18-20; ¶23-27), 2 genuine-difficulty damage zones (¶5-6; ¶22), and 1 major seam-expansion where an administrative/fivefold hypostatic taxonomy intrudes into the functional ‘tree’ teaching (¶15-17). Recommendations: excise 1 block (¶15-17); annotate none; none 5 blocks.

changes_summary: Per Finding 3 (Recommendation: excise), excised the entire seam-expansion block ¶15–17. To maintain coherent prose and paragraph sequence, ¶18 now follows directly after ¶14 and is presented here as ¶15 without alteration to its wording. No other paragraphs were modified, in line with Findings 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 (Recommendation: none).
